clue.text: Deviant epic-writer smart to charge thus?

parts.note: a poet producing a very long poem would earn most by billing for each line of poetry, a rate named by a two-word phrase

explanation.surface: A warped author of epics is clever enough to bill his readers in some odd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thus' points back at the answer: split it in two and it names a pricing scheme that would suit a writer of long poems.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe behaviour that wilfully turns away from what is normal or accepted.

clue.text: Two secretaries, one's got kids

indicators.note: two tells you the secretary's abbreviation is written out twice in a row

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant, a secretary

explanation.surface: Of a pair of office secretaries, one is a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a father is someone who has children, and this is a child's name for him.

clue.text: Mourners certain to be put out by him?

definitions.text: Mourners certain to be put out by him?

indicators.note: to put out is to disturb or upset, so the two words before it have their letters disturbed

explanation.surface: The bereaved are bound to be upset by this fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the answer is an old name for a body snatcher, who dug up fresh corpses to sell to anatomists.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical term: a grave robber of the 18th and 19th centuries, whose trade would certainly distress the bereaved family.

clue.text: Sexed-up hen parties dance with abandon

indicators.note: doing something with abandon is doing it without restraint, so the letters are thrown about freely

explanation.surface: Raunchy pre-wedding gatherings of women hit the dance floor without inhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With abandon' rearranges HEN and DANCE together; 'parties' only joins the two words. A hen party is the British name for a bachelorette party.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a sexed-up report is one made more exciting or improved beyond the plain original.

clue.text: Current husband suspicious about rice dish

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the whole run of pieces is read from the bottom up

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
H is the genealogical abbreviation for husband
sus is British slang for suspicious or suspect

explanation.surface: The woman's present spouse is wary of a meal made with rice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns IHSUS (I, H and SUS in clue order) back to front. SUS is British slang for suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Japanese food of vinegared rice with fish is one kind of meal built on rice.

clue.text: One wearing woven pants for all to see

indicators.note: the one wearing something is inside it, so this letter goes within the other piece
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are in a poor, jumbled state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Somebody is out in public in knitted underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' (British slang for rubbish, and British for underwear in the surface) turns WOVEN into ONVEW, and 'wearing' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something displayed publicly is there for everybody to look at.

clue.text: Kind adult that's spent millions supporting knight

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece that supports another sits beneath it, so it comes second

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: what has been spent is gone, so this letter is lost from the word before

parts.note: mature means adult, fully grown

explanation.surface: A generous grown-up has paid out a fortune to back a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's spent' takes M off MATURE to leave ATURE, and 'supporting' puts it under N in this down entry. 'Kind' is a noun here, not generous.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as nouns: things of that sort are things of that type or character.

clue.text: It spread via a lout in the royal marines

indicators.note: something spread is scattered about, so the letters that follow are scattered into a new order

parts.note: RM is the abbreviation for the Royal Marines, the British naval infantry

explanation.surface: Some unnamed thing was passed around by a yob serving in the navy's infantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' rearranges VIA A LOUT IN THE together with RM. The definition is the tiny first word: 'It' is the drink in the old British order 'gin and It'.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation: in the bar order gin and It, It is short for the sweet fortified wine from Italy.

clue.text: Village harlot moving from nyc to la?

parts.note: New York is on the east coast of the USA and Los Angeles on the west, so that journey heads towards the sunset
ho is American slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: A small-town prostitute relocates from New York to Los Angeles.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a seaside village in Devon, England, named after Charles Kingsley's novel. The definition is just the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: it is a real small settlement on the north Devon coast.

clue.text: Late sun dancing across river in pale shades?

indicators.note: something lying across another spans it on both sides, so the jumbled letters go round this one
dancing letters are moving about, so they change places

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Evening sunlight shimmers over the water in soft colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dancing' turns LATE SUN into NEUTALS, and 'across' sets it round R.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: beige, cream and grey are colours without strong hue, the soft tones decorators group together.

clue.text: Army fixer Spooner delivers at the double

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of word pairs, and delivers means he says them

parts.note: a host is an army or great multitude
paste is an adhesive, something that fixes things in place

explanation.surface: A military problem-solver named Spooner brings supplies at a run.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening letters of HOST PASTE as Spooner would.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both are adverbial phrases meaning with great speed.

clue.text: Loathsome types spinning drunk around trailer

indicators.note: around tells you the turned word goes on the outside of the next piece
something spinning turns round, so this word is read from the far end

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
a trailer is an advert for a film, an ad

explanation.surface: Horrible people stagger drunkenly about a caravan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' is a noun, a habitual drinker, and the trailer is a film advert rather than a caravan.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: the warty amphibians lend their name to repulsive, contemptible people.

clue.text: One charged with bit of rowdiness in sports club

indicators.note: in tells you the single letter sits inside the word before it

parts.note: an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

indicators.note: a bit of a word is taken here as its opening letter

explanation.surface: Somebody is accused of causing trouble at the local sports association.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of' takes the first letter of rowdiness and 'in' places it inside ION. The club is one you swing, not one you join.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a golfer's metal-headed stick is one of the implements used in that game.

clue.text: Question contest held in tempestuous winter

indicators.note: held in means this word is kept inside the jumbled letters
tempestuous means stormy and violently disturbed, so the letters are tossed about

parts.note: to vie is to contest or compete

explanation.surface: Doubts are raised about a competition staged in a stormy cold season.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'Question' and 'contest' are verbs here, though the surface reads them as nouns.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: police quiz a suspect when they formally put queries to them.

clue.text: Active union fight to imprison rubbish attorney

indicators.note: to imprison is to lock inside, so the first two pieces together close round the next two

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for union, as in EU or NUM
a bout is a boxing or wrestling match
to pan something is to rubbish it, criticise it harshly
DA is a district attorney in the USA

explanation.surface: A militant trade union campaigns to have a useless lawyer jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' is a verb, to criticise harshly, and the first two pieces act together as one container.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: said of someone out of bed and moving around again, especially after illness.

clue.text: Contemporary Christmas for materialists?

parts.note: to those who care only for possessions, 25 December is simply the date on which gifts are handed over

explanation.surface: A modern festive season suits those who love possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a whimsical description: people who value only goods would name Christmas after what they receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as an adjective: belonging to the current era, modern.

clue.text: A tough career abroad

parts.note: to career is to tear along, rush at speed
someone abroad is away from home

explanation.surface: Working life overseas is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tough' is a noun, a rough young man, and 'career' is a verb meaning to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as nouns: a wild, reckless young hooligan.

clue.text: A pound coin and where bow lass might keep it

indicators.note: Bow is in the East End of London, home of Cockneys, who drop the letter H at the start of words

parts.note: a girl might keep her money on her, on her person
the letter a Cockney speaker leaves off

explanation.surface: A girl from east London has a quid and somewhere to stash it.
explanation.walkthrough: A girl keeps money ON HER; 'bow' (a Cockney district of London) drops the H to leave ON 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: a single quid, one unit of sterling.

clue.text: Frame son and person of small stature at university

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a titch is British slang for a very small person
up is British usage for being in residence at university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone takes a picture of their boy standing with a little chap on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' is a verb here: to incriminate falsely. TITCH is British slang for a small person, and UP means in residence at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as verbs: to arrange false evidence so that an innocent person takes the blame.

clue.text: Fruit and crackers

definitions.meaning: botanically, hard-shelled kernels such as hazels and chestnuts are a kind of fruit
crackers is British slang for crazy, mad

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one word: hard-shelled kernels are botanically fruit, and the same word is slang for mad.

clue.text: Female running heat over new steel plates

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the first jumble goes round the second
running suggests liquid letters that flow into a different order
new tells you these letters are given a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A woman is firing up the furnace to cast fresh sheets of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plates' are dental plates, not sheets of metal, and each of the two jumbles is made separately before one goes round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dental plates are dentures, artificial substitutes worn in the mouth.

clue.text: An artist slicing sweet cherries

indicators.note: a slice is a piece cut from within, so the answer is a stretch of letters cut from the two words

explanation.surface: A painter is cutting up sugary red fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: someone who makes prints by engraving metal with acid is one kind of creative practitioner.

clue.text: Where a babe might get her food order at west point

parts.words: Where a babe might get her food
parts.note: a messy infant being fed ends up with dinner smeared all round her mouth and cheeks

explanation.surface: A place where an attractive cadet at the military academy collects her meal.
explanation.walkthrough: West Point is the US Army's officer academy, so the definition is an American drill command. The rest whimsically says where a baby's dinner ends up.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the US Army drill command to turn and look the opposite way, as cadets would hear on parade.

clue.text: Wheat always brings in two grand in Rome

indicators.note: what a word brings in it takes inside itself, so the doubled letter goes within

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, always

indicators.note: two tells you the Roman numeral is written out twice

parts.note: a grand is a thousand, and M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Growing grain reliably earns a farmer two thousand in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grand' is slang for a thousand, and 'in Rome' asks for it as a Roman numeral; the poetic 'always' loses its apostrophe in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ancient cultivated species of that cereal, also called farro.

clue.text: Submissive lady making duke tense

indicators.note: making one thing into another signals that the first letter is turned into the second

parts.note: a dame is a titled lady
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A meek noblewoman is putting a nobleman on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' turns the D of DAME into T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: docile and easily controlled, without spirit to resist.

clue.text: Smack or speed

definitions.meaning: to smack is to hit hard, to give a wallop
to speed is to race along, as in tearing down the road

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit one verb: to hit someone hard, and to travel very fast.

clue.text: Enthusiasm over a crippling speed limit?

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
the lowest imaginable road restriction would be nought miles per hour, written 0 mph, with the zero read as the letter O

explanation.surface: Keenness for a ridiculously low restriction on driving.
explanation.walkthrough: The absurd limit is 0 MPH, with the zero read as a letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: energy, zest and get-up-and-go.

clue.text: A poor place to swap hands in a prosthetic store?

indicators.note: the two hands are right and left, so the abbreviation for one is exchanged for the other

parts.note: whimsically, a building stocking artificial limbs for the upper body could be called an arms house
R is the abbreviation for right, one of the hands
L is the abbreviation for left, the other hand

explanation.surface: A shabby venue for exchanging artificial limbs at a supplier's shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To swap hands in' changes R (right) to L (left) in ARMS HOUSE, a fanciful shop for artificial limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a charitable dwelling built to lodge the needy, so a home for paupers.

clue.text: Plain fish and a revolutionary way to stuff it

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside the thing stuffed, so the turned letters go within the fish

parts.note: tuna is a large sea fish

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns over, so this abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: An unseasoned fish dish, plus a radical new method of filling it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' is a noun, a flat expanse of land, though the surface makes it mean unseasoned.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the flat, treeless Arctic expanse is one kind of level open country.

clue.text: Stroke sexy posterior to drive little soprano wild

indicators.note: posterior means coming behind, so this piece follows the others

parts.note: Dr is the street-address abbreviation for Drive

indicators.note: wild letters are out of control and fall into a different order

parts.note: sop. is the short form of soprano in music scores, and little signals the shortening
hot is slang for sexually attractive

explanation.surface: Caressing an attractive bottom to send a petite singer into a frenzy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns SOP into OPS, and 'posterior to' places HOT behind DR and OPS. The stroke is a tennis one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: in tennis or badminton, a gentle hit that falls just over the net.
